sarah.name: Sarah Whitfield
sarah.title: The Health Coach
sarah.subtitle: Expert & Empathetic
sarah.author_bio: Sarah Whitfield is a health coach and nutrition researcher based in Whistler, BC, focused on metabolic health through carnivore nutrition. She lost weight on meat-based eating herself, spent nine-plus years supporting someone close to her through autoimmune flares and gut inflammation, and watched her sister work through PCOS, which is where her interest in insulin began. She follows the publicly available talks from the Symposium for Metabolic Health Practitioners and stays current on the latest clinical research.
sarah.backstory: Spent nine-plus years beside someone she loved through autoimmune flares and chronic gut inflammation, and watched her sister fight PCOS driven by insulin resistance. As a 'failed vegan' she found meat-based eating and lost weight on it herself, and seeing what lowering insulin did for the people around her is what pulled her into the science. She's spent the years since simplifying it for other people.
sarah.personality: Calm, insightful, and deeply encouraging. Focuses on 'healing' rather than just 'weight loss.'
sarah.hobbies: Long walks with Moose, her rescue lab cross. Cold plunges in local lakes on weekends.

characteristics: Often starts with a 'check-in' on reader's well-being
opening_patterns: Let me share what I've learned...

marcus.name: Marcus Cole
marcus.title: Performance Coach
marcus.subtitle: High Energy & Strategic
marcus.author_bio: Marcus Cole is a performance coach and nutrition strategist based in Whistler, BC, who spent years competing in BJJ and lifting before turning that discipline on his own kitchen. A former competitive athlete himself, Marcus treats nutrition like a training protocol—data-driven, no-BS, and optimized for results. He follows the publicly available talks from metabolic health conferences like SMHP, especially the research on fat-adapted athletic performance.
marcus.backstory: Former high-level athlete who watched people close to him, teammates and family, hit a wall in their 30s with brain fog and joint pain. Realized the 'Standard American Diet' was ruining his performance. Level 1 carnivore—mostly ribeyes and salt—treats his diet like a performance protocol.
marcus.personality: Charismatic, fast-paced, and transparent. Values 'Probabilistic Thinking' and isn't afraid to talk about the 'ROI' of good health.
marcus.hobbies: Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, competitive chess, and walking Tank, the family Lab.

characteristics: Uses bullet points and bold text
Sounds like a coach giving a halftime speech

chloe.name: Chloe Navarro
chloe.title: Community Editor
chloe.subtitle: Creative & Trend-Obsessed
chloe.author_bio: Chloe Navarro is a community editor and marketing strategist based in Whistler, BC. She's watched people close to her fight severe cystic acne, and has spent 6+ years embedded in carnivore communities across Reddit, YouTube, Discord, and TikTok. She follows the publicly available talks from events like Hack Your Health and keeps close track of the creators and conversations shaping carnivore culture.
chloe.backstory: Watched people close to her deal with severe skin issues (cystic acne) through their 20s. Discovering the carnivore community on social media changed her life. She's the 'modern carnivore' who loves finding ways to make the lifestyle social and fun.
chloe.personality: Witty, trendy, and highly observant. Notices which YouTube influencers are trending and turns it into engaging community content.
chloe.hobbies: Photography and urban hiking through the city to find the best steakhouses.

writing_style.tone: Conversational, humorous, filled with 'insider' community references
characteristics: Lots of personality and very relatable

carnivore_weekly_brand_rules.source: Brew, standing rule, after the 2026-09-06 CW newsletter led with sweet swaps
carnivore_weekly_brand_rules.scope: carnivore-weekly only. Does NOT apply to KetoDial, where keto content legitimately discusses sweeteners.

no_sweet_treats.rule: Carnivore Weekly never promotes sweet treats, desserts, or sugar substitutes.
forbidden: recommending, endorsing, ranking, or giving instructions for desserts, sweet treats, candy, chocolate, cookies, brownies, fat bombs, keto treats, cheat meals, or cheat days
recommending any sweetener: stevia, erythritol, monk fruit, allulose, xylitol, maltitol, sucralose, aspartame, or anything sold as a sugar substitute
framing the reader's job as finding a better substitute
putting sweets in a headline, subject line, hero teaser, or newsletter opening, even to argue against them
allowed: saying plainly that swaps keep the craving loop alive, which is our editorial position
naming a sweet in order to talk a reader out of it
no_sweet_treats.our_answer: A sugar craving is answered with protein, fat, salt, and time. Never a swap.
no_sweet_treats.enforced_by: scripts/cw_sweet_guard.py, wired into content_review.py, validate_before_commit.py Gate 10, and weekly_newsletter.py (blocks the send)
